findings.current: Im Kkeokjeong, an E-rank Hunter, began sprinting at a speed beyond his ability to reach—or even properly see.
findings.defect: The sentence makes Im Kkeokjeong the person who begins sprinting, but the omitted Korean subject is Jin Taekyung; Im Kkeokjeong is the E-rank observer who cannot catch or properly see him.
findings.rationale: The preceding sentence states that Jin Taekyung vanished, and the following lines track his charge across the cavern.
findings.replacement: Jin Taekyung began sprinting at a speed that Im Kkeokjeong, an E-rank Hunter, could neither match nor properly see.
findings.source: E급 헌터인 임꺽정은 닿을 수도, 제대로 볼 수도 없는 속도로 질주를 시작했다.

findings.defect: The translation changes Taekyung’s assessment from saying the fight is manageable to merely evaluating it favorably.
findings.rationale: 할 만하다 means that something is manageable or worth attempting, which is why the remark devastates the observers after his effortless kill.

findings.current: But fights weren’t won with strength alone. I slipped inside one of them and stabbed it in the lower abdomen.
findings.defect: “Slipped inside one of them” sounds as though Taekyung entered the monster’s body and fails to convey that he penetrates its close guard or reach.
findings.rationale: 품 안으로 파고들다 describes closing into the space within an opponent’s arms or guard, not entering the opponent itself.
findings.replacement: But fights weren’t won with strength alone. I slipped inside one monster’s guard and stabbed it in the lower abdomen.
findings.source: 나는 한 놈의 품 안으로 파고들며 아랫배를 찔렀다.

findings.current: That attack just now had probably been a blow that squeezed out the last of its strength.
findings.defect: The unqualified “that attack” can refer to Taekyung’s immediately preceding stab, obscuring that the Minotaur’s own failed attack used up its remaining strength.
findings.rationale: The surrounding passage explains why the Minotaur can no longer charge: it has bled heavily and expended its remaining strength on its preceding attack.
findings.replacement: The attack it had launched moments ago had probably squeezed out the last of its strength.
findings.source: 아마 조금 전의 그 공격이 마지막 힘을 쥐어짠 일격이었을 것이다.

findings.current: “One, two, three, four… Eight of them. Forty billion in total. Wow, a few of them even dropped Magic Gems. You said all the byproducts were mine, too, right?”
findings.defect: The wager total is inflated tenfold: 40억 won is four billion won, not forty billion.
findings.rationale: Eight monsters at 500 million won each total four billion won.
findings.replacement: “One, two, three, four… Eight of them. Four billion in total. Wow, a few of them even dropped Magic Gems. You said all the byproducts were mine, too, right?”
findings.source: “하나, 둘, 셋, 넷. 여덟 마리. 도합 40억. 와, 몇 마리는 마정석도 떨궜네? 부산물도 다 내 거랬지?”

findings.defect: The literal wording is opaque in English and loses Taekyung’s rebuke that Changsoo is using disrespectfully casual speech.
findings.rationale: 말이 짧다 is an idiomatic criticism of someone speaking informally when hierarchy calls for polite speech.

findings.current: “Don’t ‘pardon’ me. You have to pay me. Forty billion.”
findings.defect: The amount owed is inflated tenfold.
findings.rationale: 40억 won equals four billion won and is the established total of the wager.
findings.replacement: “Don’t ‘pardon’ me. You have to pay me. Four billion.”

findings.current: Yet Im Changsoo talked about tens of billions of won as casually as if it were a thousand-won bill in his pocket.
findings.defect: “Tens of billions” overstates the amount under discussion and contradicts the four-billion-won wager.
findings.rationale: 수십억 denotes a sum in the billions here, specifically the four billion won being discussed, rather than tens of billions in English.
findings.replacement: Yet Im Changsoo talked about billions of won as casually as if it were a thousand-won bill in his pocket.
findings.source: 임창수는 수십억을 주머니 속 천 원처럼 말한다.

findings.defect: The response removes Changsoo’s comic mishearing of 걔 as 개, meaning “dog.”
findings.rationale: Changsoo mistakes Taekyung’s 걔야, “that guy,” for 개야, “a dog,” producing an explicit wordplay beat.

findings.defect: The generic label loses the crude, mocking force of Changsoo’s embarrassing nickname.
findings.rationale: 껄떡쇠 is a derisive comic nickname for a man who persistently lusts after or hits on women, not a neutral description.

findings.current: But since I had to collect forty billion won, I comforted him in a warm voice.
findings.defect: The amount Taekyung intends to collect is inflated tenfold.
findings.rationale: The wager totals 40억 won, or four billion won.
findings.replacement: But since I had to collect four billion won, I comforted him in a warm voice.
findings.source: 하지만 40억을 수금해야 하는 나는 따뜻한 목소리로 녀석을 위로했다.

findings.current: “You little bastard. Where do you think you’re pulling out a weapon?”
findings.defect: The translation makes the slang euphemism 연장 explicit as “weapon” and produces an unnatural English question.
findings.rationale: 연장 literally means “tool” and is used here as slang for a weapon; “that thing” preserves the deliberately indirect, contemptuous register.
findings.replacement: “You little bastard. Where do you get off pulling that thing on me?”

findings.current: It absolutely wasn’t because I hadn’t received the forty billion yet.
findings.defect: The unpaid wager is inflated tenfold.
findings.replacement: It absolutely wasn’t because I hadn’t received the four billion yet.
findings.source: 40억을 못 받아서 그런 게 절대 아니다.

findings.current: That was Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong’s lowlife-and-nasty-man combo.
findings.defect: The narration drops Taekyung’s established respectful address “Miss Song” even though the source explicitly uses 송이 씨.
findings.rationale: The source retains 씨 in Taekyung’s reference to her, and the established English address is “Miss Song.”
findings.replacement: That was Miss Song and Im Kkeokjeong’s lowlife-and-nasty-man combo.
findings.source: 송이 씨와 임꺽정의 저질, 악질 콤보에 이어서.

findings.defect: Changsoo’s reminder of the wager inflates the amount tenfold.
The translation loses Taekyung’s irritated, challenging reaction to Changsoo talking back.
findings.rationale: 어쭈 here is a confrontational interjection expressing surprise at the other person’s audacity, not a neutral request for confirmation.

findings.defect: The joking fee is inflated tenfold.
findings.rationale: 1억 won equals one hundred million won.

summary: The draft reverses the subject of Taekyung’s charge and repeatedly inflates four billion won to forty billion. It also obscures a combat mechanism, hierarchy cues, and two character jokes.
